host: Linux x86_64, 6 cores, 11.7GB RAM, shared with 3 other spike sessions; uptime 1d23h; free-m available 8.3GB at idle measurement

processes.detail: bun runner (rivetkit registry) + rivet-engine (Rust child spawned by runner, filesystem storage backend)

idle.note: measured after 20s idle, 0 actors; engine CPU is background maintenance, sampled from /proc over 20s, 6-core machine

fresh_boot.note: engine provisions its log shard and object store on first boot; ~134MB floor before any actor exists

parked_10000.note: engine RSS kept climbing during create (peak 1.69GB) then settled to ~1.24GB after ~3min; store includes log shard 143MB + objects 224MB

at_1k_parked.note: 1.3-2s spikes appear in bursts (3 of 40), p50 and most samples 3-9ms

at_10k_parked.note: no spikes in this run; sample = park, wait 300ms for sleep, then wake

kill9_survival.detail: after kill -9 of runner and engine at 1k and at 10k parked actors, restart took ~10-20s to health-ok; getOrCreate handles resolve, status/wake actions work on pre-existing keys. But c.vars (the documented in-memory vars) reset to createVars defaults: harness/sessionId/cwd/status/waitingOn/pid all lost. Durable per-session fields must go in actor SQLite (c.db), which we did not model in this spike.
kill9_survival.spawned_child_detail: spawnDetached runs /bin/sh -c CMD detached in its own process group (verified pgid == pid); child kept running after kill -9 of both runner and engine

gates.G3_pass: partial: actor identity survives kill -9; unmodeled durable fields (SQLite) expected to survive but unverified
